Expulsion of main body of Yüe-chi horde from Kan-suh by the Hiung-nū.
Nan-tiu-mi, chief of the Wu-sun, killed by the Yüe-chi.
Yüe-chi occupation of the Śaka territory ; Śaka migration.
Expulsion of Yüe-chi from Śaka territory by Koen-muo, the young Wu-sun chief, son of Nan-tiu-mi.
Reduction of the Ta-hia, both north and south of the Oxus, to vassalage by the Yüe-chi, who begin to settle down.
Dispatch by Chinese emperor Wu-ti of Chang-k'ien as envoy to the Yüe-chi.
Arrival of Chang-k'ien at Yüe-chi head-quarters, north of the Oxus.
Extension of Yüe-chi settlements to the lands south of the Oxus ; occupation of Ta-hia capital, Lan-sheu, south of the river, probably = Balkh.
Formation of five Yüe-chi principalities, including Kushān and Bāmiān.
Epoch of the Mālava or Vikrama era.
A Chinese official instructed in Buddhist books by a Yüe-chi king. (See Franke, Türkvölker, p. 92 n.)
Temporary cessation of intercourse between China and the West.
Augustus, Roman emperor, died ; Tiberius acc.
End of First, or Early Han dynasty of China.
Consolidation of the five Yüe-chi principalities into one Kushān kingdom under Kadphises I ; conquest by him of Kao-fū (Kābul), Ki-pin (Gandhāra), and Pota (? Bactria or more probably Arachosia).
Destruction of Indo-Parthian power, and gradual conquest of Northern India by Kadphises I.
Kadphises I succeeded Gondophernes at Taxila.
Buddhist books sent for by Chinese emperor, Ming-ti.
Galba, Otho, and Vitellius, Roman emperors.
Victorious career of Pan-chao, the Chinese general, in Khotan, &c.
Epoch of the Śaka or Sālivāhana era ; Kadphises I died, aged 80 ; Kadphises II Kushān (Yen-kao-ching, Wema Kadphises, &c.), his son, acc.
Defeat of Kadphises II by Pan-chao.
Reduction of Kuchā and Kara-shahr by the Chinese under Pan-chao.
Indian embassy to Trajan; Buddhist Council.
Overthrow by the Romans of the Nabataean kingdom of Petra in Arabia; rise of Palmyra.
Hadrian, Roman emperor, acc.; retrocession of Meso-potamia.
Kanishka Kushān, acc.; year 1 of his regnal era.
War of Hadrian with the Jews.
Mānikyāla inscription of Kanishka (year 18); Antoninus Pius, Roman emperor, acc.
Jūnāgaṛh inscription of Rudradāman, Western satrap.
Death of Kanishka; Huvishka Kushān, acc. as sovereign of whole empire.
Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, Roman emperor, acc.
Defeat of Parthian king, Vologeses III, by the Romans.
Foundation of Sassanian empire of Persia by Ardashīr or Artaxerxes I.
Defeat of Valerian, Roman emperor, by Sapor I.
Successful siege of Amida by Sapor II, with Kushān help.
